PullRequest.Title: Chat: align working border animation with Voice Mode
PullRequest.Body:
The in-progress chat input border now follows Voice Mode's blue-then-pink sequence while preserving the existing travel speed.

### Changes

- Run the blue listening accent for one border lap, then the pink speaking accent for one lap.
- Reuse Voice Mode's tuned rim palette while preserving explicit chat working-border color overrides.
- Respect reduced motion and replace the animated glow with a stable active-contrast border in high-contrast themes.
- Desaturate both animation phases for inactive Agents window sessions.
- Add focused regression coverage for palette reuse, phase order, motion gating, high contrast, idle state, and theme-token wiring.

### Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh` focused chat border suites — 19 passing
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- ESLint on all changed TypeScript files
- Stylelint on both changed CSS files
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- Real-workbench scenarios in Dark Modern, Light Modern, Dark High Contrast, and Light High Contrast
- Real-workbench scenarios with motion enabled and forced reduced motion
- Real-workbench scenarios at zoom levels `-1`, `0`, and `1`

Fixes #331675

### Visual evidence

Matched real-workbench captures at zoom 0. Each source run recorded the same 6.5-second in-progress state with a 276x78 chat input; the focused clips use the same crop, dimensions, and frame count.

Scenarios.Scenario: A chat request is in progress and the input working border animates through listening and speaking colors.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Request-state updates toggle the existing `working` class; CSS then animates the two pre-existing pseudo-elements. No asynchronous operation or external boundary must complete for the request or UI to progress.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One input border per simultaneously rendered in-progress chat widget, with two pseudo-elements per border. The diff preserves the same two continuously animated gradient surfaces and lap speed; it adds a second color phase within the existing animation cycle.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser animation/paint work is concurrent across visible working chat inputs; no new queue, timer, IPC, subprocess, filesystem, database, or network concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Resolved theme colors are stored as two inline CSS custom properties and reused for every animation frame until the theme changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed CSS, working-class gating, and duration calculation directly establish the animation lifecycle and cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact gradient paint cost depends on browser/GPU and visible widget count, but the diff does not increase animated-surface cardinality or angular travel rate; color interpolation is folded into the already-running keyframes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The sequence duration doubles while each lap retains its prior speed, and the same two pseudo-elements remain animated; the additional typed color property does not establish a materially larger rendering mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: The user changes color theme while one or more chat widgets exist.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The synchronous theme event invokes `updateWorkingProgressBorderColors` once per live ChatWidget, computes two colors in memory, and writes two CSS custom properties. This work is on the theme-application path but does not block any I/O or remote operation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with live ChatWidget instances, not chat history items or messages. Each instance performs a constant number of color conversions and two style writes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Theme listeners run synchronously and serially on the renderer event loop. Theme changes are user-driven and infrequent; no burst or unbounded producer is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no cross-widget cache, but each widget computes only on initial input render and theme changes, then retains the resulting strings in element styles. There are no repeated per-frame resolutions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new listener and helper call are directly visible, and the helper contains only theme lookups and in-memory color math.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The maximum number of simultaneously live chat widgets varies by workbench layout and sessions, but per-widget work is bounded and theme changes are rare.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added work is bounded, infrequent, and contains no expensive boundary or collection-wide repeated operation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reduced-motion, high-contrast, or inactive-session users view an in-progress chat input.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Request state still toggles `working`; CSS selectors suppress animation when motion is disabled and remove both pseudo-elements from display in high-contrast themes. Inactive sessions compute two desaturated CSS colors during normal style resolution.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant selector/style work per rendered chat input; animation work is absent under reduced motion and high contrast. Inactive-session desaturation adds one additional custom-property expression per input.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No application-level concurrency is introduced. Browser style recalculation follows existing class/theme changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CSS custom properties inherit/cascade normally and are recomputed only when relevant class or theme variables change; there is no cache key growth or retained collection.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: selectors explicitly gate animation on `monaco-enable-motion` and set `display: none; animation: none` for high contrast.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser-specific style resolution cost is not measured, but the changed rules are constant-size and accessibility modes remove rather than multiply continuous animation work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The accessibility paths bound or eliminate animation work, and the extra inactive-session color expression does not create meaningful scaling.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 10 changed files. Traced continuous border rendering, layout-driven duration updates, theme-change color resolution, and reduced-motion/high-contrast/inactive-session behavior. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
